title: DomainSpec integration vocabulary
goal: Define one provider-neutral vocabulary for persistence, messages, queues, topics, streams, external APIs, ORODI observation, and generated integration artifacts before implementation changes are planned.
goal_limits: Do not redefine active DomainSpec definitions D45 through D49.
Do not select providers, generate code, change compiler behavior, or claim runtime support.
Do not place provider mechanics in domain semantic types or concern-specific consumer contracts.
original_intent: Create all integration definitions first, including database, message, queue, topic, external API, and ORODI concepts.
consumer: DomainSpec language, compiler profiles, generated project layouts, runtime bindings, documentation, and future AlchLang integration declarations.

definition.normative_voice: A consumer-facing dependency contract MUST describe one responsibility and MUST NOT expose provider mechanics in its operation signatures.
definition.formal_voice: DependencyContract = (contract_id, concern, consumer_roles, operation_signatures, failure_surface, implementation_profile_ref).
definition.plain_language_voice: The application asks for a capability such as loading an order or publishing an event; it does not ask for PostgreSQL, Kafka, or HTTP details.
definition.domain_context_voice: An OrderRepository or PaymentGateway is named for the domain responsibility used by its consumer.
definition.boundary: Not a universal Port and not a provider adapter.

definition.normative_voice: A persistence binding MUST separate the logical subject, dependency contract, adapter, physical resource, implementation profile, logical-to-physical mapping, and evidence boundary.
definition.formal_voice: PersistenceBinding = (binding_id, logical_subject_refs, dependency_contract_ref, adapter_ref, resource_ref, implementation_profile_ref, logical_physical_mapping_ref, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It records how domain information reaches a database without pretending that an entity is a table.
definition.domain_context_voice: Order may bind through OrderRepository and a PostgreSQL adapter to orders/order_lines mappings.
definition.boundary: An entity is not a table; a value object is not automatically a column group.

definition.normative_voice: A transaction guarantee binding MUST state its participants, atomicity scope, selected guarantees, failure outcome binding, evidence boundary, and one local commit boundary.
definition.formal_voice: TransactionGuaranteeBinding = (binding_id, unit_of_work_contract_ref, participant_refs, atomicity_scope, selected_guarantees, implementation_profile_ref, failure_outcome_binding_ref, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It says exactly which local changes commit together and what is not covered.
definition.domain_context_voice: Saving an order and its outbox row can share a local transaction; delivering the outbox message cannot.
definition.boundary: Not a workflow and not a distributed transaction claim.

definition.normative_voice: A failure outcome binding MUST classify a boundary failure as retryable, non-retryable, or unknown without selecting the caller's continuation.
definition.formal_voice: FailureOutcomeBinding = (binding_id, boundary_ref, failure_classes, classification_rules, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It translates technical failures into stable outcomes but does not decide whether the application retries, compensates, or stops.
definition.domain_context_voice: A provider timeout may become PaymentUnavailable; the workflow still owns the next action.
definition.boundary: Classification is not control flow.

definition.normative_voice: A durable workflow runtime binding MUST compose persistence, transaction, failure, scheduler, clock, wake-up, replay, and version-compatibility bindings explicitly.
definition.formal_voice: DurableWorkflowRuntimeBinding = (binding_id, workflow_refs, persistence_binding_refs, transaction_binding_refs, failure_binding_refs, scheduler_ref, clock_ref, wakeup_ref, replay_policy_ref, version_compatibility_ref, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It states what makes a long-running workflow survive process restarts.
definition.domain_context_voice: A fulfillment workflow can resume after payment callbacks or scheduled retry wake-ups.
definition.boundary: Does not select a database, queue, scheduler, or provider.

definition.normative_voice: An integration binding MUST connect one concern-specific dependency contract or inbound application boundary to a provider realization through explicit policy and evidence references.
definition.formal_voice: IntegrationBinding = (binding_id, direction, logical_boundary_ref, contract_ref, provider_realization_ref, policy_refs, serialization_profile_ref?, failure_binding_ref, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: This is the provider-neutral join between what the application means and how an outside system is reached.
definition.domain_context_voice: OrderSubmitted publication, payment authorization, order persistence, and an inbound webhook each receive separate bindings.
definition.boundary: It is not itself a repository, message, endpoint, provider SDK, or runtime receipt.

definition.normative_voice: A provider profile MUST declare provider-specific configuration vocabulary and supported capabilities without changing logical domain semantics.
definition.formal_voice: ProviderProfile = (profile_id, concern, provider_kind, capability_set, configuration_schema_ref, secret_slot_refs, compatibility_constraints).
definition.plain_language_voice: It describes what a PostgreSQL, Kafka, SQS, or HTTP provider knows how to do.
definition.domain_context_voice: A Kafka profile can declare partition-key support while the OrderSubmitted event remains provider-free.
definition.boundary: A profile is a capability description, not an installed or live provider.

definition.normative_voice: A provider realization MUST identify the adapter and configured resource that realize one provider profile for a binding.
definition.formal_voice: ProviderRealization = (realization_id, provider_profile_ref, adapter_ref, resource_ref, configuration_ref, credential_binding_ref?, deployment_ref?, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It is the concrete configured adapter, such as this PostgreSQL database or this Kafka cluster topic namespace.
definition.domain_context_voice: ProductionOrderStore realizes the PostgreSQL profile with an OrderStore adapter and a configured resource.
definition.boundary: Configuration is not proof that the resource exists or was contacted.

definition.normative_voice: A serialization profile MUST define the stable wire or storage representation, version identifier, compatibility policy, and schema reference for a logical payload.
definition.formal_voice: SerializationProfile = (profile_id, logical_type_ref, format, schema_ref, version, compatibility_policy, encoding_options).
definition.plain_language_voice: It defines how typed domain data becomes bytes or structured data outside the domain model.
definition.domain_context_voice: OrderSubmitted v1 may serialize as JSON with a versioned schema for a topic or external API.
definition.boundary: Serialization does not imply transport, persistence, or delivery.

definition.normative_voice: A runtime receipt MUST record the bounded fact observed at an integration boundary and MUST NOT claim an effect beyond that fact.
definition.formal_voice: RuntimeReceipt = (receipt_id, binding_ref, operation_ref, observed_at, outcome, provider_evidence_ref?, correlation_ref?, claim_ceiling).
definition.plain_language_voice: It says what the runtime actually observed, such as a provider accepting a publish request.
definition.domain_context_voice: A publish receipt can prove provider acceptance but not consumer processing or business completion.
definition.boundary: A receipt is evidence of an observation, not the external effect itself.

definition.normative_voice: A persistence mapping MUST map logical subjects and value shapes to physical records, keys, fields, relations, indexes, and conversion rules without redefining the logical types.
definition.formal_voice: PersistenceMapping = (mapping_id, logical_subject_refs, physical_model_refs, identity_mappings, field_mappings, relation_mappings, index_mappings, conversion_rules, version).
definition.plain_language_voice: It explains how entities, value objects, enums, sums, lists, sets, and references are stored.
definition.domain_context_voice: Order.id can map to orders.id while Money maps to amount and currency columns and line items map to related rows.
definition.boundary: The mapping does not make the physical record the canonical domain type.

definition.normative_voice: A migration contract MUST identify source and target physical-model versions, forward steps, compatibility window, data transformation, rollback posture, and verification evidence.
definition.formal_voice: MigrationContract = (migration_id, persistence_binding_ref, from_version, to_version, forward_steps, data_transform_refs, compatibility_window, rollback_posture, verification_refs).
definition.plain_language_voice: It defines how stored data changes safely when the physical schema evolves.
definition.domain_context_voice: Adding Order.total may require a nullable compatibility phase and a backfill before enforcing a constraint.
definition.boundary: A migration changes physical representation, not domain history or semantic meaning by itself.

definition.normative_voice: A message MUST be a transport representation of a declared logical payload and MUST identify its message kind and serialization profile.
definition.formal_voice: Message = (message_type_id, message_kind, logical_payload_ref, serialization_profile_ref, version). message_kind in {event-notification, command-request, query-request, query-response, integration-document}.
definition.plain_language_voice: A message is what crosses a messaging boundary; it may carry an event, command, query, response, or document.
definition.domain_context_voice: OrderSubmittedMessage may carry selected facts from the OrderSubmitted domain event.
definition.boundary: A domain event is not automatically a message, and a message is not automatically a domain event.

definition.normative_voice: A message envelope MUST separate transport metadata from the serialized logical payload.
definition.formal_voice: MessageEnvelope = (message_id, message_type_ref, occurred_at?, produced_at, correlation_id?, causation_id?, partition_key?, trace_context?, headers, payload).
definition.plain_language_voice: It wraps the payload with identity, timing, correlation, routing, and tracing information.
definition.domain_context_voice: An OrderSubmitted payload can be wrapped with orderId as partition key and the checkout command as causation ID.
definition.boundary: Envelope metadata does not alter the payload's domain meaning.

definition.normative_voice: A message channel MUST name a logical transport destination and declare its channel kind, accepted message types, ownership, and lifecycle policy.
definition.formal_voice: MessageChannel = (channel_id, channel_kind, accepted_message_type_refs, owner_ref, lifecycle_policy_ref, provider_name?). channel_kind in {queue, topic, stream, dead-letter}.
definition.plain_language_voice: It is the logical place through which messages move, independently of its provider name.
definition.domain_context_voice: OrderEvents can later bind to a Kafka topic or another provider without renaming the domain event.
definition.boundary: Queue, topic, stream, and dead-letter channel are distinct semantics, not aliases.

definition.normative_voice: A queue MUST represent competing consumption in which an available message is assigned to one successful consumer path under the selected delivery policy.
definition.formal_voice: Queue = MessageChannel where channel_kind = queue and consumption_model = competing-consumers.
definition.plain_language_voice: Workers share the work; each message is completed by one worker path, subject to retries and redelivery.
definition.domain_context_voice: GenerateInvoice jobs may be distributed across invoice workers.
definition.boundary: A queue is not broadcast and does not imply exactly-once processing.

definition.normative_voice: A topic MUST represent publication to independently configured subscriptions, each with its own delivery state.
definition.formal_voice: Topic = MessageChannel where channel_kind = topic and consumption_model = fan-out-subscriptions.
definition.plain_language_voice: One publication can be delivered independently to multiple interested subscribers.
definition.domain_context_voice: OrderSubmitted can feed billing, fulfillment, and analytics subscriptions.
definition.boundary: A topic is not a queue shared by competing consumers.

definition.normative_voice: A stream MUST represent an ordered append log with retained positions and replay semantics within declared ordering scopes.
definition.formal_voice: Stream = MessageChannel where channel_kind = stream and consumption_model = retained-log and cursor_model is declared.
definition.plain_language_voice: Consumers read retained records from positions and may replay them.
definition.domain_context_voice: Order activity can be retained by partition and replayed by a projection consumer.
definition.boundary: Retention and replay do not make the stream an event-sourced aggregate store.

definition.normative_voice: A dead-letter channel MUST retain messages that exhausted or violated delivery policy together with failure metadata and redrive governance.
definition.formal_voice: DeadLetterChannel = MessageChannel where channel_kind = dead-letter and (source_channel_ref, terminal_failure_classes, retention_policy, redrive_policy) are declared.
definition.plain_language_voice: It holds messages that could not be processed normally so they can be inspected and deliberately redriven or retired.
definition.domain_context_voice: Malformed OrderSubmitted messages can be isolated with their validation failure evidence.
definition.boundary: Dead-lettering is not business compensation and does not resolve the failed intent.

definition.normative_voice: A publication binding MUST connect a producer contract and message mapping to one logical channel, delivery policy, failure binding, and provider realization.
definition.formal_voice: PublicationBinding = (binding_id, producer_contract_ref, logical_source_ref, message_type_ref, mapper_ref, channel_ref, delivery_policy_ref, provider_realization_ref, failure_binding_ref, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It declares how a domain result becomes a message and is offered to a channel.
definition.domain_context_voice: OrderSubmitted maps through OrderSubmittedToMessage and publishes to OrderEvents.
definition.boundary: Publication does not prove subscription delivery or consumer completion.

definition.normative_voice: A subscription binding MUST connect a channel subscription to one message mapper and application operation with explicit acknowledgement, delivery, ordering, deduplication, and failure policies.
definition.formal_voice: SubscriptionBinding = (binding_id, channel_ref, subscription_id, message_type_ref, mapper_ref, operation_ref, acknowledgement_boundary_ref, delivery_policy_ref, ordering_policy_ref, deduplication_policy_ref, failure_binding_ref, provider_realization_ref).
definition.plain_language_voice: It declares what receives a message, how it becomes typed input, and when processing counts as complete.
definition.domain_context_voice: Billing consumes OrderSubmittedMessage, maps it to CreateInvoiceInput, and acknowledges only after its local commit.
definition.boundary: A subscription is not the operation itself and transport acknowledgement is not business success.

definition.normative_voice: A delivery policy MUST declare the delivery guarantee claimed by the transport boundary, retry limits, visibility or lease behavior, and terminal disposition.
definition.formal_voice: DeliveryPolicy = (policy_id, guarantee, retry_schedule_ref?, max_attempts?, lease_or_visibility?, terminal_disposition). guarantee in {at-most-once, at-least-once} unless stronger evidence is separately defined.
definition.plain_language_voice: It states how messages may be retried or lost and what happens after delivery attempts are exhausted.
definition.domain_context_voice: OrderSubmitted may use at-least-once delivery with consumer deduplication and dead-lettering after bounded attempts.
definition.boundary: Transport delivery is not exactly-once business effect.

definition.normative_voice: An acknowledgement boundary MUST identify the observable condition after which a message may be acknowledged to its transport.
definition.formal_voice: AcknowledgementBoundary = (boundary_id, subscription_binding_ref, condition, failure_before_ack, failure_after_ack, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It says exactly when the transport is told that processing finished.
definition.domain_context_voice: A consumer may acknowledge only after invoice state and inbox deduplication state commit locally.
definition.boundary: Acknowledgement is not proof of downstream business completion.

definition.normative_voice: An ordering policy MUST state whether ordering is absent, global, or scoped by an explicit key and where that claim is observed.
definition.formal_voice: OrderingPolicy = (policy_id, mode, key_expression?, observation_boundary, disorder_handling). mode in {unordered, key-ordered, globally-ordered}.
definition.plain_language_voice: It defines which messages must be seen in sequence and which may arrive in any order.
definition.domain_context_voice: Order events can be ordered per Order.id without claiming order across all customers.
definition.boundary: Provider partition order is not automatically end-to-end processing order.

definition.normative_voice: A deduplication policy MUST identify the stable deduplication key, owning boundary, retention window, atomicity relationship, and duplicate outcome.
definition.formal_voice: DeduplicationPolicy = (policy_id, key_expression, owner_ref, retention_window, transaction_binding_ref?, duplicate_outcome).
definition.plain_language_voice: It explains how repeated delivery is recognized and handled.
definition.domain_context_voice: The billing consumer may store message_id in an inbox table in the same local transaction as invoice creation.
definition.boundary: Deduplication limits repeated handling; it does not create exactly-once delivery.

definition.normative_voice: A transport failure policy MUST map transport failures to stable failure outcomes and identify retry eligibility without selecting application continuation.
definition.formal_voice: TransportFailurePolicy = (policy_id, transport_boundary_ref, provider_failure_matchers, failure_outcome_refs, retry_eligibility, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It translates broker or client failures into outcomes the application understands.
definition.domain_context_voice: BrokerUnavailable may be retryable while InvalidMessageShape is non-retryable.
definition.boundary: It does not perform retry, compensation, or dead-letter movement.

definition.normative_voice: An inbound endpoint binding MUST map an external protocol operation to one application operation with request mapping, response mapping, authentication, failure mapping, and evidence boundaries.
definition.formal_voice: InboundEndpointBinding = (binding_id, protocol_operation_ref, request_mapper_ref, operation_ref, response_mapper_ref, authentication_binding_ref?, failure_mapping_ref, provider_realization_ref, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It exposes an application operation through HTTP, RPC, or another inbound protocol without making the operation depend on that protocol.
definition.domain_context_voice: POST /orders can map an HTTP request to SubmitOrderInput and its result to an HTTP response.
definition.boundary: An application operation is not an endpoint, controller, or route.

definition.normative_voice: An external API contract MUST describe the consumer-needed remote capability with typed requests, results, and stable failure surface, independent of protocol client mechanics.
definition.formal_voice: ExternalApiContract = DependencyContract with concern = external-api and operation_signatures expressed in domain-facing types.
definition.plain_language_voice: It is what the application needs from another service, such as authorize payment or fetch tax rates.
definition.domain_context_voice: PaymentGateway.authorize accepts PaymentAuthorizationRequest and returns PaymentAuthorizationResult.
definition.boundary: It is not an OpenAPI document, URL, HTTP client, or provider SDK.

definition.normative_voice: An external API binding MUST map one external API contract operation to a provider operation with request, response, authentication, resilience, and failure mappings.
definition.formal_voice: ExternalApiBinding = (binding_id, external_api_contract_ref, provider_operation_ref, request_mapper_ref, response_mapper_ref, authentication_binding_ref?, resilience_policy_ref, failure_mapping_ref, provider_realization_ref, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It connects a domain-facing gateway to the concrete remote API call.
definition.domain_context_voice: PaymentGateway.authorize may bind to a provider POST operation through explicit request and response mappers.
definition.boundary: A successful remote response is evidence at that API boundary, not proof of later external effects.

definition.normative_voice: A webhook binding MUST verify sender authenticity, identify replay protection, map the external notification to typed input, and define acknowledgement independently from application completion.
definition.formal_voice: WebhookBinding = InboundEndpointBinding + (sender_verification_ref, replay_protection_ref, external_event_id_expression, acknowledgement_policy).
definition.plain_language_voice: It safely accepts a callback from another system and turns it into an application input.
definition.domain_context_voice: A payment-settled webhook verifies its signature and external event ID before resuming a payment workflow.
definition.boundary: Receiving a webhook does not make the external notification a domain event.

definition.normative_voice: An authentication binding MUST bind an integration boundary to an authentication scheme, credential source, rotation posture, and disclosure-safe evidence boundary.
definition.formal_voice: AuthenticationBinding = (binding_id, integration_boundary_ref, scheme, credential_slot_refs, credential_provider_ref, rotation_policy_ref?, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It says how the runtime proves identity without embedding secrets in domain declarations or generated source.
definition.domain_context_voice: A payment API binding can use an API-key credential slot supplied by deployment configuration.
definition.boundary: The binding references secrets but never contains secret values.

definition.normative_voice: An API resilience policy MUST separately declare timeout, retry, backoff, concurrency, and circuit behavior and MUST condition retries on operation safety.
definition.formal_voice: ApiResiliencePolicy = (policy_id, timeout_policy, retry_policy, backoff_policy, concurrency_policy?, circuit_policy?, idempotency_requirement, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It defines how the client behaves when a remote API is slow or unavailable.
definition.domain_context_voice: Payment status lookup may retry safely; payment authorization may require an idempotency key before retry.
definition.boundary: Resilience behavior does not redefine business policy or failure meaning.

definition.normative_voice: An API failure mapping MUST translate protocol, provider, authentication, timeout, and malformed-response failures into the contract's declared failure outcomes.
definition.formal_voice: ApiFailureMapping = (mapping_id, external_api_contract_ref, provider_failure_matchers, failure_outcome_refs, unknown_fallback, evidence_boundary).
definition.plain_language_voice: It prevents provider error codes from leaking into application semantics.
definition.domain_context_voice: HTTP 429 may map to PaymentProviderBusy while an invalid response maps to PaymentProviderProtocolFailure.
definition.boundary: Mapping a failure does not select retry or workflow continuation.

definition.normative_voice: An integration observation MUST be an immutable, disclosure-safe account of a bounded runtime fact and MUST carry no authority to actuate the observed system.
definition.formal_voice: IntegrationObservation = (observation_id, binding_ref, operation_ref?, stage, outcome, observed_at, duration?, correlation_ref?, sanitized_attributes, evidence_refs, claim_ceiling).
definition.plain_language_voice: It is a safe fact about what happened at an integration boundary, suitable for diagnostics and evidence.
definition.domain_context_voice: An observation may record that the OrderEvents provider accepted a message after two attempts.
definition.boundary: Observation is one-way telemetry, not a command, retry trigger, database mutation, or provider effect.

definition.normative_voice: An ORODI observation binding MUST map integration observations into the ORODI evaluator through a one-way adapter and MUST prohibit any return edge to runtime control or provider actuation.
definition.formal_voice: OrodiObservationBinding = (binding_id, observation_selector, projection_mapper_ref, orodi_adapter_ref, evaluator_ref, disclosure_policy_ref, evidence_boundary) with edges runtime -> observer -> adapter -> evaluator only.
definition.plain_language_voice: It lets ORODI evaluate integration evidence without allowing ORODI to change the database, retry a message, call an API, or deploy anything.
definition.domain_context_voice: Transport failures can be projected into ORODI alert facts while retry decisions remain with the declared runtime policy.
definition.boundary: No reverse control edge, provider call, database write, retry, deployment, or external effect.

definition.normative_voice: An integration artifact layout MUST place logical contracts, bindings, provider adapters, configuration, migrations, deployment artifacts, and evidence in distinct profile-owned locations while keeping domain semantic sources provider-free.
definition.formal_voice: IntegrationArtifactLayout = (layout_id, language_profile_ref, contract_location, binding_location, adapter_location, configuration_location, migration_location?, deployment_location?, evidence_location, import_rules).
definition.plain_language_voice: It determines where generated integration code and configuration belong in each target language project.
definition.domain_context_voice: TypeScript, Python, and Rust profiles can use idiomatic folders while preserving the same semantic separation.
definition.boundary: The vocabulary fixes responsibilities and dependency direction, not one universal folder spelling for every language.

checks: All required concepts are present exactly once.
Every concept has normative, formal, plain-language, domain-context, and boundary voices.
Every reuse pins a canonical source selector and digest.
Every specialization resolves to a concept in this pack.
All source digests match current bytes.
No authority, implementation, or promotion effect is claimed.
allowed_uses: Input to a later governed design or implementation plan.
Candidate source for AlchLang integration syntax design.
Drift analysis against DomainSpec compiler profiles and runtime contracts.
blocked_actions: Compiler, schema, generator, runtime, provider, or documentation adoption.
Claims that queue, topic, stream, external API, ORODI, or multi-language generation are implemented.
challenge_or_refresh_route: Re-run Define against changed DomainSpec definitions or integration contract bytes before downstream planning.
language_application: The concepts are language-neutral. Each compiler profile may choose idiomatic names and folders only after preserving these identities, relationships, and boundaries.
claim_ceiling: Candidate integration definition baseline; no canonical admission and no implementation claim.
